data.name: Amirtha
data.gender_notes: Amirtha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amrita is the name of the elixir of immortality in Hindu mythology. The god Indra is said to have churned the ocean of milk to obtain it. It is believed that consuming Amrita grants immortality and eternal youth. The name Amirtha carries the meaning “Nectar of Immortality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amirtha usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of immortality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Blessing of eternal life and youth.
data.etymology: Amirtha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of Immortality.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amirtha total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hindi.name: अमृता
in_hindi.long_meaning: अमृत (Amrit) - अमर (Immortal) - आ (Towards) - ता (Her) - नाम (Name). Amrita means one who is towards the immortal Amrit or the one who possesses the nectar of immortality.

in_tamil.name: அமிர்தா
in_tamil.meaning: அமிர் (Amir) - தா (Ta) - ஞாயிர் (Nayir) - கள் (Kal) - ல்லத்து (Lattu) - அம் (Am) - ர் (R) - தா (Ta) - னா (Na)
in_tamil.long_meaning: Amirtam (immortal nectar) + Ta (feminine suffix) = Amirtha. Amirtha is a Tamil name derived from the Sanskrit word Amrita, which means immortal or one who possesses the nectar of immortality.

in_telugu.name: అమర్థ
in_telugu.meaning: అమర్ (Amara) - థే (The) - దే (She) - శ్ (Sha) - మృ (Mruthu) - దే (She) - దే (She)
in_telugu.long_meaning: Amara (immortal) + The + She + Sha (Goddess) + Mruthu (Nectar) + She + She = Amartha. Amartha is a Telugu name meaning one who possesses the nectar of immortality.

data.cultural_impact: Amrita is a common female name in the Hindu culture and is deeply ingrained in Hindu mythology, representing the pursuit of immortality and eternal youth. Its association with Indra, the god of rain, thunder, and the sky, adds to the name's allure, as rain is the source of life-giving water.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Amrita lies in its association with the elixir of eternal life and immortality. It represents the Hindu concept of transcending mortality and attaining a state of eternal youth and vitality. The name inspires a deep sense of longing for that which is eternal and immutable, reminding us of the ultimate goal of life: self-realization and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amirtha, meaning 'nectar' in Sanskrit, symbolizes the purity and sweetness of love and life, reminding us of the divine nectar of knowledge and bliss that sustains our spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Amrita was the name of the goddess of immortality and nectar in Hindu mythology. She is depicted as a goddess with four arms and a golden complexion. Amrita is often shown holding a pot of nectar, the elixir of life, which she distributes to the gods.

Amrita Devi, also known as Rani Lakshmi Bai, was a warrior queen who ruled the princely state of Jhansi in India during the British colonial rule. She is remembered for leading the Indian rebellion against the British East India Company during the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Amirtha, which means 'the nectar of life' in Sanskrit, is increasingly seen as an embodiment of self-care, wellness, and mindfulness in modern times. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to promoting self-care practices and creating a community for individuals seeking to improve their mental and physical well-being, using the name Amrita as a hashtag (#AmritaSelfCare). On YouTube, there are numerous videos featuring mindfulness practices, guided meditations, and yoga routines, often incorporating the name Amrita into the titles (e.g., 'Amrita's 30-day Mindfulness Challenge'). On Medium, there are articles and essays exploring the concept of Amrita as a symbol of inner peace and the pursuit of a fulfilling and meaningful life.
